issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this. The PR's stated purpose is fixing Sort-twice-on-same-Sorter behavior, but no test calls Sort twice and asserts the second result, nor asserts len(s.stack)==0 and len(s.state)==0 after iteration. Without a regression test the next refactor will silently reintroduce the bug.

issues.description: Collapsed working/walking state lacks a written invariant for the cycle-detection branch.
issues.detail: Merging working and walking into a single state changes what push()'s LastIndexFunc cycle scan relies on. The invariant that a walking node is exactly one currently on the stack is now load-bearing but unstated. Write down the state-machine spec so the cycle branch can be audited.

issues.description: Moving clear() into defer changes the reuse contract and needs documentation.
issues.detail: Original code cleared state at Sort entry; new code clears at iterator exit. If Sort is called but the returned iter.Seq is never invoked, stale state from a prior run persists. The reuse postcondition (and the reentrant-panic case, which leaves state half-cleared) should be stated explicitly on the Sorter type.

issues.description: Sorted-marker is now only set when yield returns true, changing early-termination semantics.
issues.detail: Previously s.state[k]=sorted ran unconditionally after pop; now it only runs when yield succeeds. The behavior is probably fine because the iterator is dead and defer clears state, but the state-machine change is undocumented in the commit message and the early-yield-false postcondition (partial iteration discards progress) is unstated.

issues.description: Comment typos ('visisted', 'if its') weaken the load-bearing state-machine documentation.
issues.detail: The updated comment is now the de-facto specification of the DFS two-visit invariant. 'visisted' should be 'visited' and 'if its' should be 'if it's'. A contract with typos invites readers to skim past it; tighten the prose.

issues.description: Three independent fixes are squashed into one commit; the stack-reset no-op fix deserves its own patch.
issues.detail: The diff bundles (1) collapsing working/walking, (2) fixing s.stack[0:] (a no-op that retained stale Node refs and blocked GC) to clear()+s.stack[:0], and (3) moving the sorted marker into the yield branch. Each has separate reasoning; splitting would aid bisect and review.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes real bugs: s.stack[0:] was a no-op that retained stale Node references, and the sorted-marker placement plus working/walking duplication were genuinely sloppy. The taste of collapsing two states into one and moving cleanup into defer is correct, but the simplification has outrun the documentation: the state-machine invariant is unwritten, the cycle-detection branch now depends on a subtler property, and the reuse contract (especially under early-yield and reentrant-panic) is unstated. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — add a Sort-twice regression test, write down the state invariant, fix the comment typos, and ideally split the three independent fixes.
